title: Pas encore, plus, pas assez
summary: Say not yet, no longer, not enough and not either while placing negation around the conjugated verb.
objectives: Choose negative expressions by time and degree.
Place compound-tense negation around the auxiliary.
Use `de` after negative quantities and distinguish not much from nothing.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: No longer is different from not yet
paragraphs: A negative expression denies or limits a statement. In careful written French, `ne` (`n'` before a vowel or mute `h`) precedes the conjugated verb and `pas`, `plus` or `pas encore` follows it. `Ne ... plus` means no longer/not anymore: a former situation has ended. `Ne ... pas encore` means not yet: the event is still expected. Do not add `pas` to `ne ... plus` for this ordinary meaning.

With the `passé composé`, place the negative around the auxiliary, not the participle: `elle n'a pas répondu`, `elle n'est pas encore arrivée`. Spoken French often omits `ne`; recognise `je sais pas` or `j'ai plus de pain` without treating that colloquial omission as the formal written model. Written `plus` can mean more or no longer; `ne` and context clarify the meaning.
points: `Ne ... pas du tout` strengthens the denial: not at all. `Ne ... pas non plus` adds another negative: not ... either.

examples.english: I no longer work on Saturdays.
The technician has not arrived yet.
We have not received the parcel.

examples.french: Je **ne suis pas du tout** inquiet ; elle **ne l'est pas non plus**.
examples.english: I am not worried at all; she is not either.
examples.note: Degree of denial versus adding a second negative.

mistakes.avoid: Elle a répondu pas au message.
mistakes.prefer: Elle n'a pas répondu au message.
mistakes.why: In the careful written pattern, `n'` precedes the auxiliary and `pas` follows it.

sections.title: Not enough, none left, or not much
paragraphs: `Ne ... pas assez` modifies a verb or adjective: `je ne dors pas assez`, `ce sac n'est pas assez grand`. Before a noun use `pas assez de/d'`: `pas assez de temps`. `Ne ... plus de` says a quantity is exhausted: `je n'ai plus de monnaie`. Ordinary indefinite and partitive quantities usually become `de/d'` after `ne ... pas` or `ne ... plus`; definite `le/la/les` remain.

`Ne ... pas grand-chose` means not much, not nothing. `Grand-chose` has a hyphen in this expression. `Ce n'est pas grand-chose` can minimise a problem or an amount. Do not infer zero from this phrase.
points: Compare `je n'ai pas assez de pain` (some, but insufficient), `je n'ai plus de pain` (none left), `je n'ai pas acheté grand-chose` (not much bought).
After `être`, identification retains the article: `ce n'est pas un problème`, not `ce n'est pas de problème` in that construction.

examples.english: I do not drink enough water.
The room is not big enough.

examples.note: The amount is small, not necessarily zero.

mistakes.avoid: Nous n'avons pas assez des chaises.
mistakes.prefer: Nous n'avons pas assez de chaises.
mistakes.why: For an unspecified quantity, `assez` takes `de`, not `des`.

sections.title: The emphasis can come later
paragraphs: `Pas` and `du tout` need not remain next to each other: the emphatic `du tout` can follow the object or description. `Non plus` can likewise follow the object or activity to add a second negative statement. Keep `ne/pas` around the finite verb or auxiliary even when the extra phrase comes later.
For the ordinary not-yet pattern, learn `pas encore` together before a following infinitive or participle. Do not treat every negative phrase as though its final words had the same placement options.
points: A short reply can be `pas du tout`, `pas encore` or `pas grand-chose`. In full careful written sentences, restore the appropriate `ne`.

examples.french: Je **n'ai pas aimé cette décoration du tout**.
examples.english: I did not like this decoration at all.
examples.note: `Du tout` follows the object; `pas` remains after `ai`.

examples.french: Mon collègue **ne peut pas utiliser ce logiciel non plus**.
examples.english: My colleague cannot use this software either.
examples.note: `Non plus` adds the colleague's negative situation.

examples.french: Nous **n'avons pas encore choisi** les couleurs.
examples.english: We have not chosen the colours yet.
examples.note: `Pas encore` stays before the participle in the core pattern.

practice.prompt: Make the sentence mean no longer: Je travaille ici. Use ne ... plus.
Make negative with ne ... pas: Elle a payé.
Supply de, d' or des: Je n'ai plus ___argent.
Je n'ai pas fait grand-chose means:
practice.explanation: A small amount is not necessarily zero.

practice.prompt: Use ne ... pas du tout: Je comprends. Make it mean I do not understand at all.
answers: Je ne comprends pas du tout.

practice.prompt: Use ne ... pas encore: Nous avons terminé. Make it mean we have not finished yet.
Complete with 'either' in this negative sentence: Je ne viens pas ___.
Use ne ... plus: Elle prend le train. Make it mean she no longer takes the train.
answers: Elle ne prend plus le train.

practice.prompt: Make 'no tickets left' with ne ... plus de: Nous avons des billets.
Supply the phrase 'not enough' after n'a: Il n'a ___ temps. Include de.
practice.explanation: Before a noun, use pas assez de.

practice.prompt: Supply the phrase 'not enough' before the adjective: Ce manteau n'est ___ chaud.
Supply the hyphenated expression meaning much: Elle n'a pas appris ___.
Make negative with ne ... pas: Ils sont partis.
Add not yet using ne ... pas encore: J'ai reçu la réponse.
answers: Je n'ai pas encore reçu la réponse.

practice.prompt: Supply de or les: Je n'aime pas ___ horaires proposés. Refer to the specific proposed hours.
Complete the careful written sentence by supplying the missing word: Nous ___ voulons pas attendre.
practice.explanation: Ne is expected in the specified written register.

practice.prompt: Move only du tout to the end: Nous n'avons pas du tout apprécié ce changement.
answers: Nous n'avons pas apprécié ce changement du tout.
practice.explanation: The emphatic phrase can follow the object; ne/pas still surround the auxiliary.

practice.prompt: Add non plus at the end to say that your neighbour has the same negative situation: Ma voisine ne reçoit pas ce journal.
answers: Ma voisine ne reçoit pas ce journal non plus.
practice.explanation: Non plus can follow the object without changing the main negative frame.

production_task.prompt: Explain a delay in a group project. Say what is not yet done, what resource is insufficient and what is no longer possible.
production_task.model_answer: Nous n'avons pas encore reçu les affiches. Nous n'avons pas assez de temps pour tout préparer aujourd'hui. Je ne peux plus rester ce soir, et ma collègue ne peut pas rester non plus.
production_task.translation: We have not received the posters yet. We do not have enough time to prepare everything today. I can no longer stay this evening, and my colleague cannot stay either.
rubric: Separate not yet from no longer.
Use `de` after an insufficient noun quantity.
Place negatives around auxiliaries, not participles.
